question: What is the name of the solution that is employed to identify the existence of starch in food?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Iodine solution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Iodine solution is used to test for the presence of starch in food items.
 
• When iodine solution is added to a sample containing starch, the solution changes its color to blue-black.
 
• This color change is due to the formation of a starch-iodine complex.
 
• The test is simple and widely used in both educational and laboratory settings.
 
• It is a qualitative test, indicating the presence or absence of starch rather than measuring the amount.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Starch**

 
 
• Starch is a carbohydrate consisting of a large number of glucose units joined by glycosidic bonds.
 
• It is produced by most green plants as an energy store.
 
• Common sources of starch include potatoes, rice, and wheat.
 
• In the human diet, starch is a major source of energy.
 
 
 
• **Iodine Solution**
 
 
• Iodine solution, also known as Lugol's iodine, consists of iodine and potassium iodide dissolved in water.
 
• It is commonly used in medical and biological applications.
 
• Besides testing for starch, it is used as a disinfectant and antiseptic.
 
 
 
• **Starch-Iodine Complex**
 
 
• The blue-black color observed in the test is due to the formation of a starch-iodine complex.
 
• This complex forms when iodine molecules fit inside the helical structure of the amylose component of starch.
 
• The exact nature of this complex is still a subject of research, but it is believed that the iodine gets trapped in the helical structure, leading to the color change.
 
 
 
• **Other Tests for Carbohydrates**
 
 
• Benedict's test is used to identify reducing sugars.
 
• Fehling's test also identifies reducing sugars.
 
• Barfoed's test differentiates between monosaccharides and disaccharides.
 
• Each test has a specific reagent and mechanism for detecting different types of carbohydrates.
